questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Union Government budget in India?

a. The Budget reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of people.

b. The Budget is the summary report of the financial performance of the government in power.

c. The Budget provides details of expenditures meted out by various Union Government ministries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union Government budget in India is a comprehensive financial statement that outlines the government's economic vision and policy priorities.
 
• It reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of the people by detailing plans for development and reforms (statement a).
 
• The Budget also serves as a summary report of the financial performance of the government in power, providing insights into revenue and expenditure (statement b).
 
• Furthermore, the Budget provides detailed accounts of expenditures incurred by various Union Government ministries and departments (statement c).
 
• The Union Budget is presented annually by the Finance Minister in Parliament and includes both revenue and capital budget estimates for the upcoming fiscal year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revenue Budget**

 
 
• Comprises the government's revenue receipts (tax and non-tax revenues) and the expenditure met from these revenues.
 
• Revenue expenditures are those that do not result in the creation of assets, such as salaries, subsidies, and interest payments.
 
 
 
• **Capital Budget**
 
 
• Includes capital receipts (borrowings and disinvestments) and capital expenditures (outlays on asset creation like infrastructure).
 
• Capital expenditures are aimed at enhancing the productive capacity of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**
 
 
• It is the gap between total revenue and total expenditure of the government, excluding borrowings.
 
• A high fiscal deficit indicates the government is borrowing more to meet its expenses.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget Presentation**
 
 
• The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister in the Parliament, typically on February 1st each year.
 
• The budget covers the financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31 of the following year.

questions.question: Public debt is burdensome if it ___________ future growth in output.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**reduced'.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Public debt** refers to the amount of** money owed by the government to its creditors.**
 
• When the government borrows money to finance its spending, it may have to pay interest on the debt, which can become a burden on taxpayers.
 
• However, the impact of public debt on economic growth is not straightforward. If the borrowed funds are invested in productive assets, such as infrastructure or education, they can boost future economic output.
 
• On the other hand, if the debt is used to** finance current consumption or inefficient programs**, it may not generate enough returns to justify the interest payments.
 
• Therefore,** ****public debt can be burdensome if it reduces future growth in output by diverting resources away from productive investments or by creating uncertainty about the government's ability to repay its debt.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **(magnifies) **is not a suitable term to describe the impact of public debt on economic growth. Magnification implies that the debt has an amplifying effect on growth, which may not always be the case.
 
• **(increases)** is a possible answer, but it does not specify whether the increase in public debt has a positive or negative effect on growth. Therefore, it is not a sufficient answer on its own.
 
• **(expands)** is a synonym of increases and suffers from the same limitation as option 3.

questions.question: A situation in which the government may spend an amount equal to the revenue it collects is :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** a balanced budget.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A balanced budget is a situation where the government's spending equals the revenue it collects, resulting in no deficit or surplus.
 
• It means that the government is not borrowing money to fund its expenses, and it is not saving any excess revenue for future use.
 
• A balanced budget is considered fiscally responsible and sustainable as it helps to maintain economic stability and avoid inflationary pressures.
 
• However, achieving a balanced budget can be challenging, especially during times of economic downturn or when the government needs to invest in long-term infrastructure projects.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Deficit budget: It is a situation where the government's spending exceeds the revenue it collects, resulting in a budget deficit. To cover the deficit, the government may borrow money by issuing bonds or increasing taxes in the future.
 
• Surplus budget: It is a situation where the government's revenue exceeds its spending, resulting in a budget surplus. The surplus can be used to pay off the government's debt or saved for future use.
 
• Capital budget: It is a budget that focuses on long-term investments in infrastructure, such as building roads, bridges, and schools. Capital budgets are usually separate from the government's operating budget, which covers day-to-day expenses.

questions.question: When the government’s total revenue, excluding borrowings, is less than the planned expenditure,it is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fiscal deficit**__.

__
 
• **Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure – Total receipts excluding borrowings.**
 
• **It is the amount of borrowing the government has to resort to meet its expenses.**
 
 
• **A large deficit means a large amount of borrowing.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• There are **three different types of deficit** in a budget depending upon the types of receipts and expenditure we take into consideration.

 
 
• **Revenue deficit.**
 
• **Fiscal deficit.**
 
• **Primary deficit.**
 
 
 
• **Revenue deficit = Total revenue expenditure – Total revenue receipts.**
 
 
• **It is an excess of total revenue expenditure of the government over its total revenue receipts.**
 
• In another way, **the shortfall of total revenue receipts compared to total revenue expenditure.**
 
 
 
• **Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments.**
 
 
• It is defined as the **fiscal deficit of current year minus interest payments on previous borrowings.**
 
 
 
• **Deficit financing is the budgetary situation where expenditure is higher than the revenue.**
 
 
• It is a practice adopted for financing the excess expenditure with outside resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Progressive Tax

 
 
• In progressive taxation, the tax liability increases with individual or entity income.
 
• This is based on the principle of ability to pay.
 
• Under this system, the lowest income people are generally exempted while the highest income people pay the highest taxes.
 
• Income Tax is thus an example of a progressive tax.
 
• Progressive taxation results in the redistribution of income from rich to poor.
 
• A progressive tax charges a higher tax rate for people who earn a higher income.

• Regressive Tax
 
 
• A regressive tax is when the tax rate decreases as the amount subject to taxation increases; the tax rate progresses from high to low.
 
• The lowest amount is subject to higher taxation and this leads to individuals with low income bearing the highest-burden of regressive taxes.
 
• Such tax does not take into account the ability to pay.
 
 
 
• Pay-roll tax:
 
 
• The tax that is withheld, charged, or levied on an employer's payroll is known as payroll tax.
 
• Wages, gross salary, incentives, and any other type of remuneration paid to employees shall be included.
 
• Payroll taxes are taxes that an employer is compelled to pay or withhold on behalf of his or her employees.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the term 'Public Debt'?

options.text: The total amount paid by the government to its lenders
Total revenue generated by the government
Total investment made by the government
The total amount of money owed by citizens of a country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The total amount paid by the government to its lenders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Public debt refers to the **total amount borrowed by the government** from external or internal sources to finance its expenditures and obligations.
 
• It includes loans taken by the government from **financial institutions, foreign governments, and private entities.**
 
• The government pays interest on this borrowed amount, making public debt a financial liability for the country.
 
• Public debt is broadly categorized into **internal debt** (borrowed from domestic lenders) and **external debt** (borrowed from foreign lenders).
 
• It is a critical tool for managing economic growth, funding developmental projects, and addressing fiscal deficits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Internal Debt**

 
 
• This refers to loans borrowed by the government from domestic sources like banks, financial institutions, and the public through bonds and securities.
 
• Internal debt is usually raised in the local currency and does not directly affect the foreign exchange reserves.
 
 
 
• **External Debt**
 
 
• External debt is borrowed from foreign governments, international organizations like the World Bank or IMF, or foreign private entities.
 
• It is denominated in foreign currencies, which makes it sensitive to exchange rate fluctuations.
 
 
 
• **Gross Public Debt vs Net Public Debt**
 
 
• Gross public debt includes all government borrowing, while net public debt accounts for the debt after subtracting government financial assets.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Public Debt**
 
 
• While public debt can fund infrastructure and development, excessive borrowing may lead to fiscal stress and inflationary pressures.
 
• Sustainable debt management is crucial for maintaining economic stability.

questions.question: 'Public provision' refers to those goods and services financed through the budget and:

options.text: can be used by taxpayers only
can be used only with direct payment
can be used without any direct payment
is available through online payment only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**can be used without any direct payment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Public provision** refers to goods and services that are financed through government budgets and provided for public benefit.
 
• These goods and services can be accessed **without any direct payment** by the users at the point of use.
 
• Examples include public healthcare, public education, infrastructure, and subsidized services like public transportation.
 
• The cost of such provisions is covered through **tax revenues**, ensuring equitable access to essential services for all sections of society.
 
• This approach supports the government's role in promoting **social welfare and reducing inequality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Goods:** Goods that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, meaning they can be consumed by everyone without reducing their availability to others (e.g., street lighting, national defense).
 
• **Merit Goods:** Services considered beneficial for individuals and society, often provided by the government at low or no cost (e.g., education, healthcare).
 
• **Progressive Taxation:** A taxation system where higher-income groups pay a higher percentage of their income, ensuring funding for public provisions and reducing income inequality.
 
• **Subsidies:** Financial assistance provided by the government to reduce the cost of certain goods or services, making them affordable for the general public.
 
• **Welfare State:** A concept where the government takes responsibility for the well-being of its citizens by providing essential services and ensuring a minimum standard of living.

questions.question: The Budget Division that prepares the Union Budget of India is a part of the Department of ______ under the Ministry of Finance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the department of __Economic Affairs.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance has been entrusted with the responsibility of preparation and presentation of the Union Budget to Parliament.
 
• It formulates and monitors the country's economic policies and programs having a bearing on domestic and international aspects of economic management.
 
 
• Headquarters - New Delhi
 
• Ministry - Ministry of Finance
 
• Finance Minister - Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman (As of July 2022)
 
 
 
• The Union Budget is also referred to as the Annual Financial Statement in Article 112 of the Constitution of India.
 
• It is the annual budget of the Republic of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)

 
 
• ​​DIPAM is the nodal agency of the Union Finance Ministry mandated to advise the Union Government in the matters of financial restructuring of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)
 
• It also advises the government on methods and policies for attracting investment through capital markets.
 
 
 
• Department of Financial Services
 
 
• ​​The Department of Financial Services (DFS) supervises several key programs, policies, initiatives, and reforms of the Government concerning the Banking Sector, the Insurance Sector, and the Pension Sector in India.
 
• Initiatives and reforms relating to Financial Inclusion, Social Security, and Insurance as a Risk Transfer mechanism are also monitored by this agency.
 
 
 
• Department of Revenue
 
 
• ​​The Department of Revenue functions under the overall direction and control of the Secretary (Revenue).
 
• It exercises control in respect of matters relating to all the Direct and Indirect Union Taxes.
 
• Such control is exercised through two statutory Boards namely:
 
 
• The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) - Monitoring laws governing Income Taxes.
 
• The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) - Monitoring laws such as Goods and Service Tax, Customs, etc.
